P01-012.challenge_claim: One item challenges (high) that the one-unit warrant rests on a blanket no-imperative and no-addressee-shift statement the pointed bytes contradict twice inside the span; that the doubled ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.3.19, the verse the rejected rival turns on, is undisclosed; that the rival is dismissed on a translation-side ground with its Hebrew pivot unquoted; and that splice and gloss extents part company at oshb:Jer.3.12. The paired item supports the same entry, holding that neither the imperative at Jer.3.12 nor the call at Jer.3.14 carries a fresh addressee, formula, or scene change, and that the Jer.3.19 rival was correctly declined.
P01-012.grounds: Same object, opposite dispositions, and the bytes decide for the challenge. boundary_rationale claims that no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides the restoration promise and the reflection from the invitation that opens the unit; two of its three terms are byte-false. אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) is a fresh feminine-singular imperative, and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) is a fresh plural imperative with a fresh plural vocative against the feminine-singular addressee of שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier). The plural second person in fact already stands inside the earlier verse's own tail, וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) - one verse earlier than the challenge locates the shift - and the second witness renders all of it number-blind. The third term holds: no word-event formula and no messenger-formula onset falls inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20, so the cure is a re-cut of the negative, not its reversal. The variant point holds too: the inventory carries two notes at MT 3:19, one of this book's twelve doubled-note verses, and the bytes give תקראו תִּקְרְאִי and תשובו תָשֽׁוּבִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) - two second-person number alternations sitting on exactly the addressee question the cohesion sentence gets wrong, in the one verse the rejected alternative is built on, disclosed in no field. No count, slice, or rendered quotation covers that verse, so the mechanical disclosure arms stay silent there; the omission is material on content, not on the machine. The rival is raised on the rendering's fresh quotation mark, a tier-4 signal that is never evidence, while the Hebrew pivot at that verse, וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) - the emphatic independent pronoun the entry names but never quotes - goes unweighed. Extent: the Jer.3.12 splice stops on the bound noun of נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), severing it from the divine name, while the rendering beside it runs to the end of the verse; a second extent miss, named in neither item, runs the other way at the onset, where the splice carries the speech-introduction frame וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) that its rendering omits. High severity is proportionate: the failed sentence is this unit's own cohesion warrant, and every further leg lands on the same addressee question.
P01-012.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the blanket negative with a positive cohesion warrant - the single divine speech opened at Jer.3.11 runs on with no onset formula anywhere inside the span - and state the imperative at Jer.3.13, the imperative-with-vocative at Jer.3.14, and the singular-to-plural addressee turn explicitly, with the disposition that keeps them inside the unit. device_notes: disclose the two variant notes at MT 3:19 (single-witness; a doubled-note verse), naming both as second-person number alternations, since the contested addressee reading and the rejected rival both stand on that verse. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-argue the Jer.3.19 rival from its emphatic pronoun-plus-perfect pivot rather than from the rendering's quotation mark, and name the closer rival at Jer.3.14; one sentence plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence only. Splices: re-cut the Jer.3.12 pair so the rendering opens and closes where the splice does and no splice terminates on a construct severed from its nomen rectum, and extend the Jer.3.11 rendering to cover the speech-introduction frame the splice already carries. Tests the cure must pass: no negative claim about imperatives or addressee inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20 survives that the pointed bytes contradict (the test that killed the original); every variant verse the entry argues from carries its disclosure; each splice and its rendering share their opening and closing words. A re-span at Jer.3.14 is a PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit boss adoption - it is not author work.

row.boundary_rationale: The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a comparative statement, then pivots into command: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) — “Backsliding Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah” (web:Jer.3.11), continuing directly into הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier) — “Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, you backsliding Israel,’ says Yahweh; ‘I will not look in anger on you, for I am merciful,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will not keep anger forever” (web:Jer.3.12) — a go-and-proclaim imperative carrying the shuv invitation. The promised restoration (shepherds, the ark forgotten, Jerusalem as Yahweh’s throne, Judah and Israel reunited: web:Jer.3.15-18) and Yahweh’s own reflection on disappointed hope (web:Jer.3.19-20) continue inside the same continuing speech, since no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides them from the invitation that opens it. A narrated scene shift — a voice heard weeping, rather than reported divine speech — opens the next unit at Jer.3.21.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at the emphatic pivot opening web:Jer.3.19 was considered, since the WEB rendering opens a fresh quotation there; it was rejected for lacking a word-event formula, koh-amar onset, or imperative of the kind that bounds this book's other seams, so the reflection is kept inside the larger invitation-and-promise unit at reduced confidence rather than split on that softer signal alone.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A narrated scene, not reported divine speech, opens this unit: ק֚וֹל עַל שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.3.21, byte tier) — “A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the children of Israel; because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten Yahweh their God” (web:Jer.3.21) — shifting from the first-person divine promise of the preceding unit to third-person description of a sound. A conditional address to ‘Israel’ by name, resuming Yahweh’s own voice, opens the next unit at Jer.4.1.

P02-001.challenge_claim: Two distinct items. One challenges (medium) a register lapse: pipeline part-and-row vocabulary standing in place of the literary self-reference, said to repeat across all four prose fields. The other challenges (medium) the parenthesis denying any address or formula shift at Jer.4.7 - holding that the second person turns from plural to feminine singular there and the speaking voice moves with it, while the entry keeps high confidence on that denial - and adds that the variant note at oshb:Jer.4.5 is placed on this unit's opening imperative when it sits on the verse's third imperative.
P02-001.grounds: Distinct defects, not one: register on the one side, byte claims on the other. Both are real, and each item's own count-object needs correcting. Byte leg, upheld: the summons commands a plural throughout - הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier) and שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) - while Jer.4.7 turns to feminine-singular suffixes, אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ (oshb:Jer.4.7, byte tier), a change consonantally certain in the final kaf where a plural addressee would carry mem; and the voice moves with it, from divine first person at כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) through third-person description to a first-person-plural speaker naming YHWH in the third person at כִּ֥י לֹא שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier), before the divine formula returns at Jer.4.9. The formula half of the denial holds - no onset formula stands at Jer.4.7 - so the parenthesis fails on address, not on formula, and it survives only in the second witness, which is number-blind there and is tier-4 ground that is never evidence. The variant locative in device_notes is byte-false as well: the note at MT 4:5 rides on ותקעו תִּקְע֥וּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier), not on the verse-opening imperative that carries this unit's own warrant, while boundary_rationale states the same note correctly - so the entry contradicts itself across two fields. Correcting that item's own object: the qere sits on the fourth imperative form of the verse, third only under a bare-imperative object the item did not name. Register leg, upheld in substance with its object corrected: the pipeline vocabulary stands in three prose fields, not four - boundary_rationale (a writer part named as the thing that opens, and a following unit called a fresh row), strongest_rejected_alternative (a candidate split called its own row), and device_notes (three further uses) - while literature_type_guess is clean. Both cross-unit mentions do carry their verse anchors (Jer.4.10, Jer.4.7), so the verse-anchoring requirement is met and what remains is the workflow noun itself, headed by the part-level self-reference, where the sanctioned self-reference is the literary unit. The machine register arm does not fire on these strings, so the cure is an authored rewording rather than a validator-driven fix. Disclosure elsewhere is sound: the variant at MT 4:5 is disclosed and the pointed qere is the form quoted, the petuchah at MT 4:8 is the correct type and correctly held non-driving, and no paseq falls inside Jer.4.5-Jer.4.9.
P02-001.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the part-level self-reference and both row-nouns with this unit's own self-reference, keeping the verse anchors; and replace the parenthesis at Jer.4.7 with the byte state - no onset formula there, but the second person turns from the plural of the summons to feminine singular, and the voice has moved to a first-person-plural speaker by Jer.4.8. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-argue the declined cut at Jer.4.7 against that number-and-voice turn, not only against the absence of imperative, vocative, or messenger formula; one sentence plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence. device_notes: correct the locative - the note at MT 4:5 sits on the trumpet imperative, not on this unit's opening imperative - and drop the remaining workflow nouns. confidence: re-derive it once the rival is weighed; high is not proportionate while the closest rival is declined on a denial the pointed suffixes contradict. Tests the cure must pass: no negative claim about address at Jer.4.7 survives that the pointed suffixes contradict (the test that killed the original); no field names a writer part or a row; and the variant locative matches the inventory's note position in both fields that mention it. A cut at Jer.4.7 is a PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit boss adoption.

Jer.4.5 carries a ketiv/qere note (the unpointed ותקעו stands before the qere it repeats); the row quotes the qere reading תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier), “Blow the trumpet in the land!” (web:Jer.4.5). The imperative frame runs through the third-person invader description at Jer.4.7 (no address or formula shift there) and the further sackcloth-imperative at Jer.4.8, closing on the neum-corroborated consequence for the ruling classes at Jer.4.9, “the heart of the king will perish” (web:Jer.4.9); the neum tag there is closure corroboration (non-driving), since the next fresh tier-1 onset (the prophet’s own first-person speech-attribution at Jer.4.10) opens a fresh row rather than continuing this one.

The circumcise-your-heart imperative of web:Jer.4.4 closes this unit and this span together; a discourse-frame imperative (‘declare and blow the trumpet’) follows beyond this span.

P02-007.challenge_claim: (a) Both challenges: the rejected alternative enumerates why neither Jer.4.29 nor Jer.4.30 opens a fresh unit but is silent on the first-person turn at Jer.4.31, a comparable ground it never names or rules out. (b) One challenge adds: the markedness asserted for the pronoun at Jer.4.30 is attached to the quoted qere when the consonantal divergence belongs to the ketiv the row expressly sets aside.
P02-007.grounds: (a) is ONE AND THE SAME defect in both challenges, and it is upheld: כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי heads oshb:Jer.4.31 (byte tier), a turn to first-person perception, and strongest_rejected_alternative names only Jer.4.29 and Jer.4.30. Both framings need one correction, which does not disturb the finding: the 'same class of marker' they invoke BLENDS three byte-distinct shapes - a speech-attribution finite verb (וָאֹמַ֞ר at oshb:Jer.4.10, וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי at oshb:Jer.5.4), an exclamatory outcry (מֵעַ֣י מֵעַ֨י at oshb:Jer.4.19) and a vocative to the deity (יְהֹוָ֗ה verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.3), none of them a perception verb; the object must be named per shape before the class carries weight. The supporting cross-seam ties are byte-true: the two-word sequence at oshb:Jer.4.19 and oshb:Jer.4.31 stands at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:18 = WEB 9:19) and the first-person soul noun token-bound at 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses, MT keys), both sites among them - though the far end lies two units back, making this a long-range tie rather than an adjacent-seam device. (b) UPHELD exactly. The inventory records 1 variant note at MT 4:30, and the source writes the unpointed ketiv ואתי immediately before the pointed qere וְאַ֨תְּ (both source bytes; the pointed qere is byte tier). The divergent member - one final yod - is carried by the KETIV the row sets aside: token-bound that skeleton stands at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:2 = WEB 9:3) against 110 verses for the qere skeleton (sweep: 110 verses, MT keys - homograph-blended, a floor on ordinariness, not a pronoun census). The form the row quotes and calls unusual and marked is the common one, and neither witness marks it as unusual. The onset is sound and uncontested: the subordinated formula shape at oshb:Jer.4.27 is attested at 29 verses (sweep: 29 verses, MT keys) and the frame owner does change across the front seam. Mark handling is complete and correctly typed: setumah at MT 4:26 on the front seam, petuchah at MT 4:31 on the closing verse, types not conflated, single-witness and non-driving both stated, the MT 4:30 note disclosed, and no paseq seg recorded in the span.
P02-007.remedy: In strongest_rejected_alternative for Jer.4.27-Jer.4.31, add Jer.4.31 to the enumeration and dispose of it on its own bytes, naming the shape exactly - a first-person perception verb after the two-word voice sequence, NOT a speech-attribution formula - and stating why it does not open a fresh unit inside a formula-opened oracle. In boundary_rationale, re-attach the markedness sentence to the ketiv: state that the note's consonantal divergence is carried by the unpointed ketiv, that the pointed qere the splice quotes is the ordinary form, and strike 'unusual, marked'. If the long-range tie to Jer.4.19 is argued in prose, add web:Jer.4.19 to boundary_evidence_refs. PROPOSAL ONLY, explicitly NOT author work: a cut at Jer.4.31 separating the death-cry from the formula-opened oracle is flagged for boss adoption and must not be executed inside this remedy. P02-017.challenge_claim: No byte claim in the row is false and the seam stands, but three defects: the English gloss set beside the Jer.6.6 splice covers neither end of what was spliced, dropping the four-word formula that opens it and adding a mound clause the splice does not contain; the formula the warrant rests on is a subordinated shape opening on a causal connective, quoted but not engaged, against the bare verse-initial formula at Jer.6.9, and the two are separate objects book-wide (29 verses against 153); and the frame-owner change that actually makes Jer.6.6 an onset, the besiegers' cry giving way to divine speech, is left implicit when a formula warrant owes the mouth.
P02-017.grounds: Re-derived from the source bytes. The row's splice is the first seven words of MT 6:6 and re-collates at byte tier (oshb:Jer.6.6). Limb one is upheld and is the load-bearing defect: the English set beside that splice covers neither end of it. The splice opens on כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), five words the gloss renders not at all, while the gloss's tail, “and cast up a mound against Jerusalem” (web:Jer.6.6), answers וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), four words that stand later in the verse and are not inside the splice. Fidelity is not the problem - the English is verbatim against the staged receiving text and carries its ref in the same field - the problem is extent, in both directions, and the unglossed head is exactly the formula the warrant rests on. Limb two is REFUTED on the bytes: the connective-plus-formula shape is attested at 29 verses book-wide (sweep: 29 verses, MT keys) and stands verse-initial at 28 of them, the one non-initial site being MT 24:8, so at MT 6:6 it is the book's standard subordinated-onset shape and not a buried subordinate clause; and the 29-verse shape is a strict subset of the 153-verse formula census (sweep: 153 verses, MT keys), a shape within its superset rather than a separate object. MT 6:6 also carries the plain armies title, a member of the 50-verse formula-plus-title set (sweep: 50 verses, MT keys), so both recorded substrate-signal keys are byte-correct here; the bare verse-initial כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.6.9, byte tier) is a second onset three verses on, not a standard the seam fails. Limb three REFINES: the incoming mouth is in fact given - the splice carries the divine name and title and the prose calls the speech divine - so what is missing is the OUTGOING frame owner, the attacking force's own summons at ק֖וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה (oshb:Jer.6.4, byte tier) and ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַלָּ֔יְלָה וְנַשְׁחִ֖יתָה (oshb:Jer.6.5, byte tier), which both witnesses render in the first person plural as the attackers' own speech; the ruled granularity licenses this cut on a frame-owner CHANGE, and the change is asserted without the party being changed from ever being named. NEW FINDING, raised by neither item: the ground given for rejecting the strongest rival is byte-inexact at the exact verse the rival would cut. The rival is answered by saying the closing imperative is addressed to the same city already under address, but at MT 6:6 the city is governed by a preposition and is then spoken OF in the third person at הִ֚יא הָעִ֣יר הָפְקַ֔ד (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), the verse closing on בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), and MT 6:7 continues third-person of her, whereas MT 6:8 names her as the vocative of a directly addressed imperative, הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier), with second-person suffixes at מִמֵּ֑ךְ and אֲשִׂימֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier) that both witnesses render as address to the city. The addressee therefore CHANGES at MT 6:8, which is the ruled tier-1 explicit-addressee-shift class - the rival's live ground, and the one the row never answers. Verified sound and not disturbed: the setumah at MT 6:5 on the front seam and the petuchah at MT 6:8 on the row's own close are both correctly typed, kept apart, and held tier-3 single-witness non-driving; the inventory records exactly 1 variant note at MT 6:7 and the bytes bear it out, the unpointed reading standing immediately before the pointed one, disclosed without being quoted; and span-relevant disclosure symmetry is complete - the chapter's paseq segs stand at MT 6:1, 6:11, 6:14 and 6:16 (inventory: 4 segs in the chapter, 0 in span), and the inventories carry 0 special letters and 0 exegesis notes anywhere in MT 6:6-6:8. The seam stands; nothing here moves it.

P02-021.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defect claims and they do not both survive. Item (b) is UPHELD. oshb:Jer.6.18 summons שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם and, under its own imperative, וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה; oshb:Jer.6.19 summons שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ while its body speaks of הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה in the third person; oshb:Jer.6.20 then turns to second-person-plural possessors עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ and וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם, rendered “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices are not pleasing to me.” (web:Jer.6.20). That suffixed burnt-offerings spelling stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, oshb:Jer.6.20 and oshb:Jer.7.21), and at oshb:Jer.7.21 it is unambiguously the people's own cult addressed under the full divine-title stack - so reading the possessors at 6:20 as the summoned nations and earth is not what the bytes support, and the rival-rejection sentence asserts exactly that. The same addressee-shift class is what cuts this unit's front seam, so the criterion is applied inconsistently and the internal turn is disclosed nowhere. The consequence particle opening oshb:Jer.6.18 (sweep: 55 verses book-wide; 3 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.6.15, oshb:Jer.6.18, oshb:Jer.6.21) binds the summons back to the refusal reported at oshb:Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17 and, unlike oshb:Jer.6.21, carries no formula overriding it; with neither weight weighed, high confidence is not calibrated. The boundary itself is not decided here.

The row closes on oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6, שִׁבְתְּךָ֖ בְּת֣וֹךְ מִרְמָ֑ה בְּמִרְמָ֛ה מֵאֲנ֥וּ (oshb:Jer.9.5, byte tier) — ‘shivtekha betokh mirmah,’ ‘your dwelling is in the midst of deceit,’ a ne'um-YHWH close followed immediately by a fresh koh-amar onset at 9.7.
